title: Evading Community Detection via Counterfactual Neighborhood Search

problem.claim: Users may need to hide their community membership to preserve anonymity while remaining on a platform.

contributions.claim: Formulates community membership hiding as a constrained counterfactual graph objective.
Solves the formulated objective using deep reinforcement learning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments report that the method outperforms existing baselines.
The method is reported to achieve the best balance between accuracy and cost.

narrative_sequence.summary: Community detection helps social media platforms identify tightly connected groups with shared interests.
Community detection can expose users' tastes or affiliations, motivating anonymity-preserving opt-out behavior.
Community membership hiding alters network structure to prevent selected nodes from being identified by a community detection algorithm.
The study uses a constrained counterfactual graph objective solved with deep reinforcement learning.
Experiments compare the method with existing baselines on accuracy and cost.

source_observation.claim: A privacy-preserving intervention is framed as selectively altering graph structure to prevent community-membership identification.

interpretation.claim: Graph structure can be treated as an intervention surface for controlling the visibility of inferred attributes.

application.claim: This framing may apply to systems where users need to reduce exposure to graph-based inference while preserving platform participation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which graph edits, constraints, algorithms, or deployment settings are required.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the graph-editing operations or constraints.
The abstract does not report datasets, metrics, baseline identities, or numerical results.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
